dedupe_keys.name: grazer simulation and optimal control of coupled gas and power networks and other network dynamical systems

description: Grazer is open software for the simulation and optimal control of dynamical systems defined on networks, introduced in a paper by Eike Fokken, Simone Gottlich and Michael Herty on efficient simulation of coupled gas and power networks under uncertain, stochastically fluctuating demands and supplies, tested on networks of realistic size. The repository README explains that inputs are JSON files validated by JSON schemas, that it is built with CMake using gcc or clang 9 or later on Linux and macOS with dependencies such as METIS, and that it offers a command-line interface with run and schema subcommands and a test suite. Example runs simulate a gas-power network and solve an optimal control problem for compressor and valve use on the same gas network. The code is written in C++ and available under the MIT licence as a free download from GitHub, with releases built by continuous integration. Coverage is not tied to a region. Caveats: the author states it is used and tested by one person and has rough edges, macOS builds are no longer checked automatically, and Windows support is not maintained. Simulation uses are transient coupled gas and electricity network flow and control studies, including stochastic demand. Related records: model-gasnetsim and model-simone-gas-pipeline-simulation also simulate gas networks.
